chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from more than one of our companions from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who has a female slave, and his wife annoys him and is jealous of her, so he says to her, 'She is a charity upon you.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he dedicated her for the sake of Allah and mentioned Allah, then it is not for him to approach her (for intimacy). And if he did not mention Allah, then she is his slave girl, and he does with her what he wishes.'

key_terms.يَصْنَعُ بِهَا مَا شَاءَ: he does with her what he wishes

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of mentioning Allah's name when a husband dedicates his slave girl to his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal mechanics of *tabarru'* (dedication) within the context of concubinage, distinguishing between a religious vow and a simple transfer of property based on the explicit invocation of Allah's name. It highlights the juristic principle that the spiritual weight of the dedication determines the wife's authority (*tamlik*) over the slave, thereby resolving domestic disputes through a clear legal framework. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intention (*niyyah*) and verbal specification in transforming property rights.
